title: Ironveil fulfillment integration notes (scratch)
body:
Meeting purpose: quick capture from 2024-10-03 sync w/ Ironveil (fulfillment ops) — raw notes, open questions, action items. Not polished; for internal handoff and next-call prep.

Attendees (Redwood): Priya Nair (lead SE), Miguel Ortega (infra), Ethan Park (runtime); (Ironveil): Laura Chen (CTO), Raj Patel (Head Fulfillment), Ana Gomez (SRE).

High-level customer ask:
- Replace current homegrown heuristic routing (rules engine) with LLM-powered routing + re-ranker for pick/pack exception routing and ‘priority assignment’.
- Hard SLOs: 95th percentile decision latency <= 120ms end-to-end (API-in -> routing-decision-out) at 150 qps sustained, 300 qps burst for 5m.
- Data residency: EU-only for order metadata (customer EU region).
- Need audit trail for all decisions (user id + input payload + model version + tokens + scores) retained 90 days.
- No raw PII allowed to leave their VPC; must integrate with KMS and allow on-prem/private deployment.

Current infra notes (from them):
- Kubernetes cluster on Azure (EU-West) with a private subnet, egress through NAT; they want Redwood Private (VPC) deployment initially.
- Existing service takes CSV order batches -> synchronous HTTP call to routing service. Typical payload ~2.2KB (compressed ~0.8KB), 120–160 tokens after tokenization (we measured locally).
- Peak concurrent requests hit 320 qps during promo windows.

Technical constraints / gotchas we surfaced:
1) Latency budget is tight: 120ms E2E at 95p includes network hop + model inference + any DB lookups. For Private deployment we need to co-locate inference nodes in their private subnet or ensure single-hop routing via peering.
2) Batch vs sync trade-off: Continuous batching can reduce cost but increases tail latency. For their routing use-case they prefer deterministic latency so suggest small batching (batch size 1–8) and fast RT kernels.
3) Tokenization mismatch: They use pre-tokenized scoring in some places; need to verify tokenizer alignment with model (we recommended BPE-compatible model, we flagged off-by-one tokenization on long SKUs).
4) Embedding store integration: they plan to use self-managed Milvus (same VPC). Need connector for vector lookup inside VPC; confirm whether we should proxy queries through Redwood control plane or allow direct private endpoint.
5) Audit logging: they need per-decision logs + model metadata. Discussed using Redwood Console export hooks -> forward to their S3 (EU). Need to validate retention + size estimate (150 bytes metadata + ~payload size) -> ~150MB/day estimated.
6) Failover behavior: on model/infra failure want deterministic fallback to rule-engine (their existing). We need safe, deterministic fallback API that returns both reason and which fallback triggered.
7) Cost sensitivity: They asked for monthly cost estimate for 150qps sustained. We gave a ballpark and promised a more detailed cost breakdown for Dedicated vs Private.

Model/serving decisions we discussed:
- Candidate families: small LLM (e.g., Llama2-13B-8k quantized) for routing decisions + a tiny re-ranker (7B or distilled) for tie-breakers. Reason: routing semantics are brittle to hallucination if model too large/unconstrained; smaller model + prompt template + structured output safer.
- Need output strict schema (JSON with fields: route_id, score, confidence_bucket) and a validation layer in Redwood runtime to reject malformed outputs.
- KV/prefix caching: pattern is repetitive (same flow for many SKUs), recommended prefix caching of 3–10 prompts; Miguel to validate memory footprint on 16GB GPU host.

POC success criteria (what Ironveil will accept):
- Decision accuracy >= their current rule-engine + X% (they want at least no regression; target improvement 8–12% fewer manual exceptions).
- 95p latency <= 120ms for steady state 150 qps (measured in their env).
- End-to-end audit logs pushed to S3 within 30s of decision.
- Transparent cost report showing per-decision token cost and infra amortized cost.

Open questions (we must answer before next sync):
- Q1: Can Redwood Private be deployed into their existing AKS private subnet without changing their egress model? (Action: Miguel to confirm network prerequisites + NAT interplay)
- Q2: Does the Milvus instance support TLS mutual auth? If not, do they want Redwood to manage a proxy? (Action: Raj to confirm Milvus config; Ana to share connection JSON)
- Q3: Exact tokenization test vectors for 20 representative orders (to validate token counts). (Action: Priya will request sample set)
- Q4: Audit retention projection at 90 days — they need an SOC/finance estimate for storage cost. (Action: Samira to produce storage cost calc)
- Q5: What default fallback rule set should we map to when model confidence < 0.3? (Action: Laura + Raj to provide their current rule thresholds)

Immediate next steps and owners (rough deadlines):
- Miguel: network feasibility doc + minimal port list + VPC peering checklist (due 2024-10-10).
- Priya: collect 20 sample order payloads, run local tokenization w/ suggested model tokenizer, share summary (due 2024-10-06).
- Samira: draft audit/logs export prototype (console export to S3) and storage cost estimate (due 2024-10-14).
- Ethan: quick runtime benchmark (quantized 13B vs 7B re-ranker) on 4xA10 (multi-tenant contended) to estimate 95p latency at batch=1..8 (due 2024-10-11).
- Raj/Laura (Ironveil): confirm Milvus TLS config + provide fallback rule doc (due 2024-10-09).

RISKS / assumptions (call out to PM/SE):
- Assumption: payload sizes remain ~120–160 tokens; if future payload templates change (rich customer messages) latency/cost will shift. Need schema contract.
- Risk: Private deploy networking misconfig could add 20–40ms e2e for NAT hops; must avoid extra hop.
- Risk: Their SRE headcount limited; prefer seamless ops (we should consider managed export and onboarding assistance).

Notes to self (SE handoff):
- Keep prompts tiny and programmatic; use structured prompt + few-shot examples to avoid hallucination.
- Build a validation shim in the client adapter: if model returns malformed JSON, return fallback and log incident with full output + model version. Create a GitHub issue to track this adapter.
- Check PR #7 in repo (linked) — it's a starting point for on-prem connector. Add unit tests for TLS handshake and S3 export flow.

Planned next call: 2024-10-17 09:00 CET — agenda: present Miguel network doc, Priya tokenization summary, runtime quick-bench, agree POC plan and MOU.

Free-form / misc scribbles:
- Consider a tiny multi-model routing table: cheap 7B for routine decisions, 13B for complex exceptions; route by complexity score computed at edge.
- Could explore offloading embedding similarity to their Milvus to reduce token overhead (embed smaller context windows).
- Keep cost model transparent: supply per-route token count estimate with optimistic/realistic/pessimistic buckets.

End of notes.

-- Priya Nair (SE)
